_note: Four recovered or new mechanics, one per level type. `extract` and `reckon` come back from v1's Abjad Tower with better grounding than they had; `assay` is the thing v1 did better than v2 and is being taken back; `station` is Yūsuf Ascent's Station Point rebuilt out of language instead of optics. Checked by verify_levels.mjs, which asks a different question of each type.

levels.name: The Doomed Letter
levels.brief: Write all three letters, then every nūn is taken out of the word. Two must still be standing afterwards.
levels.teaches: Isolating a letter DETACHES it; it does not delete it. So a letter resting on the pier can never be extracted at all — it just sits there joined to nothing — and a letter the word is carrying falls, and takes whatever hung on it. Put the nūn where it carries nothing.

levels.name: Name the Number
levels.brief: One number will bring this span down. Read the values and find it.
levels.teaches: Composing words whose abjad sum equals a chosen number is the technique; here the run that sums to the number you name comes apart, and gravity does the rest. Read the values off the blocks — and remember that a sun letter has already changed the one before it.

levels.name: The Assay
levels.brief: You are standing in one of the five metaphysics and you are not told which. Run the probes, read what happened, and name it.
levels.teaches: v1 hid which scheme was operative and made you discover it by building. v2 put the ruleset in a panel, which is right for a workbench and wrong for a puzzle. This takes it back: the rulesets genuinely disagree, so their disagreements are evidence.

levels.name: The Station
levels.brief: These letters are one body. From which direction do they read as القلم — the Pen?
levels.teaches: Yūsuf Ascent asked you to find the one viewpoint from which scattered fragments compose a picture. That needs a camera moving through space. This is the same puzzle made of writing: a body is ordered by projection onto the reading direction, so the same structure genuinely spells different things read different ways.

probes.label: Write رم — does the word break at the rāʾ?
Speak م — is the spoken register admitted at all?
Write مه — does a two-letter program do anything?
probes.reads: whether a minimum procedure length is demanded

probes.label: Write الم — three luminous letters. How strong?
Write اب — abjad 1 and 2, a perfect ratio. How strong?
